lines.say: The deadlift. Here's what it really works.
Your glutes and hamstrings pull your hips forward.
The muscles along your spine keep your back flat.
Your upper back and your grip hold the bar.
But aren't deadlifts bad for your back?
In one trial, people with back pain who trained deadlifts improved about as much as those doing gentle exercises.
The key is form. Bar close to your legs, back flat, push the floor away.
Start light, and add weight slowly.
